breadcrumb: 23. Jordan Papé, CEO, The Papé Group (Individual, Eugene)
tldr: Jordan Papé, CEO of The Papé Group, argues that Oregon's substantial natural and economic advantages are undermined by man-made barriers: restrictive land-use regulations, high taxes, underperforming K-12 education, and slow development approvals. He urges a fundamental reorientation toward growth-oriented planning, creation of a Commerce Department, comprehensive tax reform, regulatory streamlining, and K-12 improvement to restore Oregon's investment competitiveness.

bullets.text: Oregon ranks 7th highest regulated state nationally, with unique statewide zoning, Urban Growth Boundaries, and Exclusive Farm Use designations creating multiple layers of development vetoes
K-12 NAICS ratings are in bottom decile despite per-student funding 50% above pre-Measure 5 levels (inflation-adjusted) and teacher pay in top quartile
Oregon ranks last in economic development funding while ranking high in homelessness funding, creating fiscal unsustainability
Proposes shift from restrictive to growth-oriented land-use system backed by 3-5 biennia budget forecasting to generate needed state revenue
Recommends removing additional state-level wetlands restrictions on properly zoned land within UGBs that have already completed public review
Advocates comprehensive tax reform to reduce income and estate taxes, which deter capital investment
Proposes creation of Department of Commerce to oversee investment mandates, review regulatory barriers, and propose modernization
Recommends sunset requirements for administrative rules and programs with thorough cost-benefit review before renewal
Calls for reform of prevailing wage requirements and expanded shovel-ready industrial and commercial land funding
